about: The 291 rivers as lines: where each runs as drawn, and the water it carries at every point. Drawn as the picture drew them, they give the river pixels of Water.png exactly.
order: Largest first: id 1 carries the most water. A river is listed after the river it joins.

fields.ends_in: sea, river (it joins the river whose id is in joins), or salt lake (the desert's two rivers)
fields.sea_rank: for a river that reaches the sea: its place among those by the most water it carries, 1 the largest (the numbering of Features.md's table of rivers)
fields.largest_flow_m3s, flow_at_end_m3s: the most water it carries anywhere, and what it carries at its end: where it reaches the sea, the river it joins or the salt lake's shore. They are the same but for the seven rivers that lose water crossing the Desert or the Grassland
fields.length_km: along the line, as far as the land of Continent.png goes
fields.from_kingdom, to_kingdom, kingdoms: the kingdoms of KingdomMap.png at its first point, at its last point on land, and all it touches. A river that is itself a border touches both its kingdoms all the way
fields.from_lake: the lake of LakeMap.png it flows out of, if its line starts at a lake's outlet
fields.lakes: the lakes of LakeMap.png its line passes through, in order
fields.points: [x, y] in pixels of the map, about 1.5 px apart, from where the river is first drawn to its end. A river that reaches the sea runs on some 9 px past the land's edge, to be cut off where the coast is drawn; a river that joins another ends on that river's line
fields.flow_m3s: the most water it has carried so far at each point: its flow, but never less than upstream, so that a river losing water to its bed is drawn no narrower for it. DrainageFlow.png has the flow itself, cell by cell
fields.width_px: its width at each point by the rule below
fields.drawn_px: the width the pictures draw it at each point: width_px rounded to a whole number of pixels
fields.course: [x, y], the river's bed as it was routed over the land: the middles of the half-size cells of DrainageDirection.png it runs through, before it was smoothed and made to wander. This is the line that runs downhill on Elevation.png

which_are_drawn: A stream is drawn where it carries 15 m3/s or more. The stream out of a lake of 60 km2 or more is drawn too, however small, down to the next river or the sea: 32 rivers begin so, carrying less than 15 m3/s at first.
width_rule: width_px = 1.3 + 1.25 * (flow / 40) ** 0.36, a quarter more in swamp and tropical rainforest country (7 and 9 on TerrainMap.png), and never under 2 or over 12
how_drawn: Each point is drawn as a disc drawn_px across, and the points are joined. On the pictures with the hand-drawn coast a river is cut off 3 px beyond the land.
wandering: A river's line is its course smoothed, then swung from side to side where its bed is nearly level (not at all where it falls 2.5 m in a km or more), in loops about a dozen widths long.
left_out_fields: The 14 river lines the water was worked out as that are too short to draw: why, where each starts ([x, y]), the water it carries, its length from cell to cell, and where it ends.
